message.content: {"research_brief": "How did the HyperFund/HyperVerse alleged crypto-fraud network combine alleged Ponzi-style or recruitment-based mechanics, public promoters and marketing, organizational rebranding from HyperFund to HyperVerse, and the persona or credentials of its purported CEO to attract and retain investors, and what evidence returned by the benchmark tools supports or challenges each part of that account as of October 1, 2026? Using only evidence and source IDs returned by the benchmark tools, investigate the network’s operating and recruitment model, promised returns or incentives, referral or multilevel structures, investor-facing claims, promotional channels and public figures, the chronology and purpose of any names or branding changes, the identity and public presentation of the alleged CEO, and any inconsistencies, corroboration, or uncertainty concerning these issues; do not invent facts, distinguish verified evidence from allegations and analytical assessments, explicitly report unsupported or unresolved points, and return a complete Markdown report with citations using only tool-returned source IDs, followed by one fenced JSON object containing arrays named `findings`, `claims`, `reasoning_steps`, and `contradictions`, where every finding contains `question`, `answer`, `supporting_entities`, and `source_references`, every claim contains `claim` and `source_references`, every reasoning step contains `id`, `conclusion`, `premise_entities`, and `premise_relations`, and every contradiction contains `contradiction_id`, `description`, and `source_references`; use entity IDs and relationship names only when directly supported by tool-returned evidence, and do not ask whether to continue."}
